subject: Dedicated capacity options and conservative min-floor path for LedgerCore
messages:
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@ledgercore.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity options and conservative min-floor path for LedgerCore

Hi Samira —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Attached is a compact options packet (ledgercore_dedicated_options_v3.pdf) that lays out three practical paths we discussed for dedicated capacity sizing tied to your launch window. I pulled the numbers against the usage profile you shared (chat-heavy inference with periodic batch embedding runs). High-level summary here so you can skim: 

- Option 1 — Conservative min-floor (recommended short-term): 8-GPU reserved cluster (4xA100-80GB-equivalent lanes) with a 12-week warmup ramp to 24 GPUs. Provides a low-cost baseline while enabling predictable latency for production. Includes prefix caching and a burst policy to hosted spare capacity for <10% traffic spikes.
- Option 2 — Balanced throughput: 24-GPU reserved cluster with staged activation: 24 -> 48 over 6 months. Better for sustained throughput and reduces per-token unit economics.
- Option 3 — Aggressive capacity: 48-GPU baseline for enterprise throughput with reserved burst windows and priority scheduling.

Key tradeoffs called out in the attachment: min GPU floor (how many GPUs must be reserved to guarantee SLO), cold-start warmup plan (how we pre-warm KV & embeddings), and a suggested activation cadence tied to your product milestones (alpha, beta, GA). I also included a short warmup simulation (warmup_simulation_v2.xlsx) that shows expected token throughput and cold-cache cost during the first 12 weeks.

Next steps I recommend: pick a primary option + a 6–12 week conditional ramp trigger (e.g., sustained request rate > X r/s or revenue milestone). If you want, we can include a short onboarding credit and an SLA carve to cover the first 30 days of warm-up. Marissa is CC'd and can confirm margin for onboarding credits.

Do you want a quick call tomorrow to walk through the spreadsheet and anchor a preferred option?

Thanks,
Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
attachments: ledgercore_dedicated_options_v3.pdf (21 pages), warmup_simulation_v2.xlsx (tabbed model), redwood_onboarding_credit_terms.pdf
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@ledgercore.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement <procurement@ledgercore.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 10:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity options and conservative min-floor path for LedgerCore

Dev —

Thanks for the packet. High level questions after a first pass:

1) For Option 1 (8 -> 24 over 12 weeks), what is the minimum guaranteed throughput per GPU you model? We need to understand worst-case latency if traffic scales quickly during beta.
2) How does the burst routing to hosted spare capacity work for PHI-sensitive requests? We need to ensure nothing leaves our VPC when the fallback triggers.
3) Procurement asked for a clear timeline and an activation penalty / decommit window. They want to know if we commit to 8 GPUs, what flexibility we have at month 3 and month 6.

Procurement is looped to start on commercial language. We should get a follow-up with specific guardrails we can show leadership.

—Samira
Head of ML Systems, LedgerCore
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@ledgercore.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity options and conservative min-floor path for LedgerCore

Samira —

Great questions, answers below (I pulled the numbers from the workbook tab “min-floor assumptions”):

1) Modeled per-GPU baseline: we assume 22–26 tokens/s for chat-style inference (decoder-only large model) on an A100-80GB-equivalent lane with continuous batching + KV cache. Worst-case tail latency (95th) when underrun occurs is ~220–300ms per token at 8-GPU scale; with 24 GPUs that drops to ~70–100ms. The attached spreadsheet shows the throughput curves and tail-latency sensitivity for RPS moments.

2) Burst routing: for PHI-sensitive traffic we can configure an isolation policy — we will not route PHI-labeled requests to hosted spare capacity. The fallback policy we propose for Option 1 will only route non-sensitive, best-effort requests to the hosted pool. That policy is applied at the request tag level and enforced by our private control plane in your VPC. I added a short note in the packet (page 17).

3) Flexibility / decommit windows: for the 8-GPU commitment we can offer a staged decommit schedule:
   - Month 1–3: firm 8-GPU baseline (standard early-termination applies)
   - Month 4–6: option to step down to 6 GPUs with 30 days' notice and a modest decommit fee (10% of remaining commit for the step-down window)
   - After month 6: re-evaluate against actual usage; we can include a one-time re-benchmarking credit to avoid unnecessary overcommit.

Also: Marissa has visibility on a limited onboarding credit we can attach to the first 45 days to help cover warm-cache inefficiencies.

If that reads clean, we can convert Option 1 into a term sheet and route to procurement. Would procurement prefer that in a tracked DocuSign link or as a redline-ready PDF?

Best,
Dev
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@ledgercore.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity options and conservative min-floor path for LedgerCore

Samira / Dev —

Quick note from finance & CS: we can authorize a one-time onboarding credit equivalent to 2 weeks of baseline committed spend for Option 1 (applied as a billing credit across the first 60 days). We'll also approve the PHI isolation clause (no fallback for PHI tags).

On the commercial language: LedgerCore is a strategic target for our payments vertical — I'm fine to greenlight a more flexible Month 4 step-down (6 GPUs) with a 10% step-down fee as Dev outlined. Procurement: please flag any contract clauses you need different here and we'll do a quick redline.

-Marissa
VP, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@ledgercore.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement <procurement@ledgercore.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity options and conservative min-floor path for LedgerCore

Marissa / Dev —

This looks good — thank you. Procurement will prepare a purchase order reflecting: Option 1 (8-GPU baseline with a 12-week ramp to 24 GPUs), onboarding credit, the Month 4 decommit flexibility with the 10% step-down fee, and explicit PHI isolation (no hosted fallback for PHI). We'll send a PO and initial legal redlines by Friday.

One small ask: can you include a short 1-page runbook for the warmup phase (operational steps we need to run in weeks 0–4) so our SREs can start prepping infra? If you can attach that as a separate doc (or add a one-pager to the hub link), that would be ideal.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Samira
